newsitem.title: FRANCE: BOF Governor Trichet sees euro launch in 1999.
newsitem.headline: BOF Governor Trichet sees euro launch in 1999.

text.p: Bank of France Governor Jean-Claude Trichet said on Thursday he was "more than ever" confident that a single European currency would be launched in 1999.
"It seems to be me the euro is more than ever on track to be launched on January 1, 1999," he told French LCI television.
Trichet, commenting on the new government's deficit-reduction plan announced this week, said he shared Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn's sentiment that the French economy was picking up.
"He has the sentiment that the economy's picking up -- I share that sentiment," Trichet said.

The plan entails 32 billion francs in budget cuts or 0.4 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), to allow France to fulfill the criteria for monetary union. Twenty-two billion will come from higher taxes and 10 billion from savings.
Trichet said the Bank's monetary policy council had recommended cutting the deficit "and the plan goes in this direction."
The plan aims to push France's public deficit down towards three percent of GDP this year, the target set by the Maastricht treaty to establish a single European currency.
"I am confident that if a further effort were needed ... to fully meet the criteria ... the necessary decisions would be taken," he said.
